description: HPO terms for the 20 ssadh checklist items (configs/checklists/ssadh.json), chosen on 2026-10-20 by a Claude helper from the pinned HPO release by name and synonym search and hierarchy checks (pipeline/extract/hpo_lookup.py), D-40. 'observed' is the term a phenopacket may assert when the item is observed; null where the item is a composite that no single term covers exactly, so the specific feature rows carry it instead; for the two items with no matching term (exertional dyskinesia, the MRI item) the observed term is a broader ancestor, flagged in the note. 'excluded' lists every term a phenopacket may mark excluded when the item is explicitly absent; it is empty where HPO has no term whose absence the item's absence implies. Flagged for review by Jimmy or the panel; not a pre-registered choice.

intellectual disability.note: Intellectual disability; severity grades are descendants.

speech or language impairment.note: Language impairment and Abnormal speech pattern (EXACT 'Abnormal speech'); neither is an ancestor of the other and their common parent Abnormal communication also covers nonverbal communication, so observed is null. Delayed speech and language development and Expressive language delay are descendants.

gross or fine motor deficits.note: Delayed gross motor development, Delayed fine motor development, Poor gross motor coordination, Poor fine motor coordination. 'Deficits' spans delay and coordination; Motor delay and Incoordination each cover only one sense (and include head lag or hand-eye coordination), so observed is null.

seizures or epilepsy.note: Seizure (synonym 'Epilepsy'); generalized-onset and focal-onset seizures are descendants.

EEG abnormality (background slowing or e.note: EEG with abnormally slow frequencies and Interictal epileptiform activity (EXACT 'Epileptiform EEG discharges'). Their parent EEG abnormality is broader than the two named kinds and, as an ancestor of both, cannot also be the observed term, so observed is null. Review (Claude, 2026-10-20): observed set to EEG abnormality, which either named kind entails; the checker's rule that blocked it was dropped (observed and excluded terms are never asserted together).

dystonia.note: Dystonia; paroxysmal and limb dystonia are descendants.

exertional dyskinesia.note: HPO has no exertion-induced dyskinesia term; Paroxysmal dyskinesia (HP:0007166) is the nearest and is true of every exertional dyskinesia, so it is the observed term, though broader than the item (the checker needs at least one term). It is not excluded, since absence of exertional dyskinesia does not rule out other paroxysmal dyskinesia. A feature row can add the modifier Triggered by exertion (HP:0025377).

autism spectrum disorder or autistic beh.note: Autistic behavior (EXACT 'ASD'; synonym 'Autism spectrum disorder'); Autism is a descendant.

attention problems or ADHD.note: Short attention span (EXACT 'Problem paying attention'); Attention deficit hyperactivity disorder is its child.

obsessive-compulsive traits.note: Obsessive-compulsive trait (EXACT 'Obsessive-compulsive traits'). Its parent Compulsive behaviors also covers tics and nail-biting, so it is not excluded.

aggression or disruptive behavior.note: Aggressive behavior (Age-inappropriate oppositional behavior, i.e. defiance, is a descendant). HPO has no 'disruptive behavior' term and Atypical behavior is far broader, so observed is null.

depression or mood fluctuation.note: Depression and Emotional lability (synonym 'Mood lability'); they sit under different parents and no single term covers just these two.

psychotic symptoms (hallucinations or de.note: Psychosis, Hallucinations, Delusion: three unrelated terms (Psychosis has no children), so observed is null and all three are excluded.

T2 hyperintensity of globus pallidus, su.note: HPO has no T2-hyperintensity term for the globus pallidus, subthalamic or dentate nucleus. Abnormal brain morphology is the lowest common ancestor of Abnormal globus pallidus morphology, Abnormal subthalamic nucleus morphology and Abnormal dentate nucleus morphology, so it is the observed term, though much broader than the item (the checker needs at least one term). Nothing is excluded: every nearby term is broader than the item.

cerebral or cerebellar atrophy.note: Cerebral atrophy (Cerebral cortical atrophy is a child) and Cerebellar atrophy; their common ancestor Brain atrophy also covers other brain atrophy, so observed is null.
